run.question: The payment-api pod in namespace app-101 had issues on November 23, 2026 around 13:45 UTC. What happened?

report.summary: The app-101 payment-api pod did log real failures starting right at the reported time, but the evidence does not reach a root cause. Loki holds the pod's application log (job=payment-api, service=payment-api, pod payment-api-101-8486559b69-6qrwv, file /var/log/payment-api.log). A complete query of that stream for 2026-11-22T12:00Z–2026-11-23T18:35Z returned 46 lines with none omitted: everything before 13:46 is INFO 'Payment processed successfully', the last such success being 13:42:00Z, and the first failure is ERROR 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' at 2026-11-23T13:46:00Z (wait_time_ms=1227, queue_length=10). Eight such pool-exhaustion errors occur between 13:45 and 14:45 (13:46, 13:54, 14:03, 14:15, 14:19, 14:21, 14:31, 14:44), with wait_time_ms reaching 4840 ms at 14:21 and queue_length between 5 and 15, while some payments still succeeded (13:59, 14:49, 15:27, 17:01, 17:38). So the pod's own failure signal is database connection-pool exhaustion appearing within one minute of 13:45. What produced it is unresolved: the payment-api Deployment/ReplicaSet/Pod no longer exists (namespace app-101 now holds only Deployment loki and pod loki-66445c6d6f-rrclp), so its env/DB-pool settings and pod status could not be read; no database workload or DB logs are visible in the cluster or Loki; and every Prometheus and Jaeger call returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error-rate, request-rate, latency or trace data exists for this window. Candidate causes (pool-config change, database-side slowness, request surge) each remain unverified hypotheses. No enabled fault-injection setting was found: all flagd flags, including paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable, are at defaultVariant off. Note for data provenance: a payment-api-101 pod was created at 18:34:43Z and its containers killed at 18:34:55Z, five hours after the incident window, and is not tied to the 13:45 failures.

claims.text: Loki logs for namespace app-101 come only from pod payment-api-101-8486559b69-6qrwv (labels job=payment-api, service=payment-api, filename=/var/log/payment-api.log); the query {namespace="app-101"} over 2026-11-22T12:00:00Z–2026-11-23T18:35:00Z returned 46 lines with lines_omitted 0.

The last line before the first failure is INFO 'Payment processed successfully' at 2026-11-23T13:42:00Z, and the first failure is ERROR 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' at 2026-11-23T13:46:00Z with wait_time_ms=1227 and queue_length=10 (only non-success line in 12:30–13:50).

Eight lines containing 'pool exhausted' fall between 13:45 and 14:45 on 2026-11-23 (13:46, 13:54, 14:03, 14:15, 14:19, 14:21, 14:31, 14:44), all level=ERROR from pod payment-api-101-8486559b69-6qrwv; wait_time_ms peaks at 4840 (14:21) and queue_length ranges 5–15.

Before 13:46 every line returned for that window (2026-11-22T12:14:00Z–2026-11-23T13:42:00Z) is level=INFO 'Payment processed successfully' with no ERROR lines, and successful payments also appear during the error period at 13:59, 14:49, 15:27, 17:01 and 17:38, so the service kept succeeding intermittently while pool-exhaustion errors occurred.

In the complete 46-line set the newest pool-exhaustion line is 14:44:00Z; the only later lines returned are successes at 14:49, 15:27, 17:01, 17:38 and INFO 'Payment API started' (port 8080) at 18:34:44.232190Z.

At query time there is no payment-api workload object left to inspect: the cluster-wide Deployment list contains no payment-api/payment-api-101, namespace app-101 holds only Deployment loki (1/1 available, created 18:34:22Z) with ReplicaSet loki-66445c6d6f and pod loki-66445c6d6f-rrclp, and no payment-api Service exists.

app-101 events between 18:34:22Z and 18:34:55Z show Deployment payment-api-101 scaling ReplicaSet payment-api-101-8486559b69 from 0 to 1, that ReplicaSet creating pod payment-api-101-8486559b69-6qrwv, its containers (payment-api, promtail) starting at 18:34:43–18:34:44Z, and both containers 'Killing' at 18:34:55Z — about five hours after the 13:45 failures.

No database workload is visible for payment-api: the deployment list at 18:36:04Z contains otel-demo application services, loki (app-101) and clickhouse (app-222) but no database serving app-101, and a Loki query {namespace=~".+"} for 13:30–15:00 returned only the app-101 payment-api streams.

A separate entity exists in another namespace: Deployment payment in otel-demo (1/1 available) with pod payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm started 2026-11-23T14:36:29Z; it is not the app-101 payment-api pod and was created after the 13:45 window.

The fault-injection flags in otel-demo's ConfigMap flagd-config (demo.flagd.json) are all at defaultVariant 'off', including paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable, so no enabled fault setting was found in the ConfigMaps that exist now.

A restart or rollout of the payment-api pod at ~13:45 is rejected as the immediate explanation: the only 'Payment API started' line in the complete 46-line log set is 18:34:44.232190Z and no startup line appears near 13:45, while payment log lines continue across 13:42.

Candidate 1: payment-api's own database connection-pool configuration (e.g. a reduced pool size applied around 13:45) exhausted the pool — unverified, because the Deployment/ConfigMap holding that setting no longer exists and change history is not integrated.

Candidate 2: the database side (slowness or unavailability holding connections until acquisition failed, with waits growing to 4840 ms) caused the exhaustion — unverified, because no database workload, database logs or database metrics are observable in this environment.

Candidate 3: a surge in payment request volume exhausted a fixed-size pool — unverified, because no request-rate, error-rate or latency metrics could be read (Prometheus unreachable) and the returned log lines are too sparse (46 lines over ~30 hours) to measure traffic.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable for this Run: metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names, get_label_values, get_prometheus_target and list_prometheus_rules all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error-rate, request-rate, latency or kube-state metrics exist for payment-api or any database.
Jaeger was unreachable for this Run: traces_list_services and traces_search returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no trace evidence exists for the 13:45 window.
The payment-api-101 Deployment/ReplicaSet/Pod no longer exists, so its container env (DB host, pool size), pod phase, restart count and last termination reason/exit code could not be read.
No database component and no database logs are present in the queried cluster or Loki, so the identity and health of the failing dependency are unknown.

A Loki query {namespace="app-101"} |= "pool exhausted" for 14:45–18:35Z returned no lines (no_data); that does not prove the condition ended, especially since the log averages roughly one line per 20–90 minutes.

No information on what configuration, if anything, changed around 13:45: the change_history integration is not_integrated and no manifest history, deployment revision or managed-fields trail for payment-api exists.

It is unexplained why pod payment-api-101-8486559b69-6qrwv was created at 18:34:43Z and killed at 18:34:55Z; the events show only controller create/start and container 'Killing', and no restart or exit reason is recorded.
next_steps: Retrieve the payment-api-101 Deployment manifest and its revision history (Git/CI) for the minutes before 2026-11-23T13:45Z to see whether DB pool size, connection timeout or DB target changed.
Inspect the payments database server's own metrics and logs (connections, max_connections, lock/latency) for 13:30–15:00Z to test the database-side hypothesis.
If available, compare load-generator/request-rate for payment-api at 13:45Z against an earlier baseline to test the volume-surge hypothesis.
Restore or authorize Prometheus and Jaeger access before drawing conclusions about error rates and latency; no metric or trace evidence was obtainable in this Run.

Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
